2) Redline exchange on Clause 4 roles and the routing language.
3) If needed, confirm whether you want the dedicated-capacity option on the Order Form (we can provision via Dedicated offering, subject to purchase).

From: Maria Gomez <legal@medtechco.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medtechco.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs: transfer resilience & order form mapping

Irene — thanks for the package and the clear callouts. A few items from our side after a quick review of Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx and the SCC mapping:

1) Transfer Impact Addendum: given our requirement to demonstrate that PII never leaves the EEA for processing and our internal risk committee guidance, we will need a Transfer Impact Addendum that captures routing commitments and fallback behavior. Annotated SCCs alone won't cover the governance evidence we require.

2) Clause 4 (roles): we have a concern with the current phrasing that could be read to allow limited controller-like processing (e.g., behavioral profiling for R&D). We will propose language that keeps profiling for product improvement within strictly aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry — we will send specific redlines.

3) Dedicated capacity / EU-only processing: procurement would like a contractual commitment that production inference for MedTechCo-controlled datasets is restricted to EU regions. If Redwood can offer an EU-only processing SKU (either Dedicated or a virtual routing guarantee), include costs and lead time.

4) Evidence request: please provide KMS key locations, current EU subprocessor list, and an ETA for the subprocessor inventory export. We will expect evidence within 10 business days after agreeing the DPA addendum.

Attached: MedTechCo_SCCs_annotated.pdf (comments inline).

Can your legal ops and product confirm feasibility? If dedicated capacity is required it will impact procurement timelines — we are trying to avoid a full on-prem procurement if an EU routing guarantee suffices.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
General Counsel
MedTechCo

I'll propose a single consolidated email back with (a) draft Transfer Impact Addendum, (b) Clause 4 redlines, (c) order form note for EU-only processing as an optional line item and provisional DocuSign link for the Order Form so they can lock commercial while DPA redlines are finalized.

Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA / SCCs: transfer resilience & order form mapping — proposed language

Thanks — drafting suggestions below (high level). I've attached a short doc with snippets (proposed_DTA_routing_snippets.docx).

Proposed Clause 4 redline (roles):
"Processor (Redwood) shall process Personal Data solely on behalf of and in accordance with Controller's documented instructions. Processing for product improvement, model training, or aggregated telemetry shall be strictly pseudonymized and limited to aggregated metrics that cannot be attributed to an identified individual. Redwood shall not engage in behavioral profiling of Controller's data absent explicit Controller authorization."

Proposed Transfer Impact Addendum (summary):
- Contractual commitment to route Controller-designated production inference traffic to EU regions (EU-West-1 / eu-central-1 equivalent).
- Dedicated logical routing guarantee: if EU-region availability is constrained, Redwood will (a) route to a pre-approved EU-compatible model variant or (b) place traffic in a queue until EU capacity is available.
- Optional Dedicated SKU: dedicated capacity for customer's production workload available at negotiated commercial terms (lead time ~ 4–6 weeks).

Commercial note: we should avoid promising guaranteed physical isolation unless the customer purchases Dedicated. The DTA can offer routing guarantees and fallbacks, plus an optional purchase path to Dedicated capacity.

Please let me know if Laura wants edits to the liability/indemnity cross-ref (I redlined a limiter to exclude indirect profits in the draft).

Karthik
